real_qa.q: How should you identify and approach national lead generation clients as a rank-and-rent operator?
real_qa.r: Start by looking at what's already happening in America through platforms like PaperCall, which show affiliate offers and the types of services people are paying for like locksmith, roofing, and concrete. Then search those keywords in your local area to find companies that are outliers—those scaling ahead, hiring more people, advertising, with good reviews and call centers. The best approach is to prepare by getting leads and traffic first, then contact them with proof of results rather than a cold pitch.

real_qa.q: Why do exact match domains still work effectively for local SEO despite industry skepticism?
real_qa.r: Exact match domains work because they directly tell Google and LLMs what a website is about. They're not a cheat code to compete with massive authority sites, but they work well in niches where the first page isn't dominated by high DR pages. Google wants to show both big expanding websites and smaller mom-and-pop shops that have been around, so they can't apply hard filters on DR or backlink metrics without losing real businesses. The skepticism may stem from Google's own misinformation rather than actual algorithm behavior.

real_qa.q: What unique data points should you include in location-based lead generation pages to avoid Google penalties?
real_qa.r: Include hyperlocal information unique to each area rather than generic sales copy templated across all pages. Examples include nearby amenities like bus stations or 7-Elevens, local neighborhood names, suburban area references, nearby national parks, regional regulations, grants, or legalities specific to that location. You can use ChatGPT to brainstorm what potential customers in that region would want to know, and scrape or buy regional data to create these unique identifiers that signal to Google you're providing location-specific value.
real_qa.requete: What unique content lead generation local pages need

real_qa.q: Why is local SEO more resilient than affiliate and SaaS SEO in the face of Google algorithm updates?
real_qa.r: Local SEO is more resilient because it operates differently from affiliate and SaaS keywords. While info keywords and affiliate sites got hit hard by updates like the information keyword update that affected HubSpot and others, local lead gen sites have been ranking for 13 years using old techniques—some even with duplicate content pages—and are still performing. The nature of local business demand and the difficulty in applying broad algorithm filters without losing legitimate local businesses makes this vertical more stable than the high-competition affiliate space.
real_qa.requete: Why is local SEO more resilient than affiliate SEO

real_qa.q: What AI tools and processes does Will Tribe use instead of traditional SEO optimization software like Surfer SEO for lead gen content?
real_qa.r: Will uses Codex with ChatGPT, Claude CLI for adversarial reviews, and OpenRouter to connect cheaper Chinese AI models for content creation. He doesn't use Surfer SEO because lead gen pages are all different and don't require consensus on specific keywords like affiliate or high-competition niches do. Instead, he uses basic optimization—including keywords in titles, H2s, and naturally throughout—and provides Codex with competitor examples from Ahrefs and LSI keyword data to guide content structure.
